baseline: Sets, natural numbers, elementary logic and finite arithmetic; no arbitrary advanced primitive vocabulary.

finite-set.description: A set X is finite if it is bijective with {1,…,n} for some natural number n≥0; its cardinality is n.

binomial-coefficient.description: For integers 0≤k≤n, binom(n,k) counts the k-element subsets of an n-element set and equals n!/(k!(n−k)!).

zagier-involution.description: For a prime p≡1 (mod 4), let Sₚ={(x,y,z)∈ℤ₊³:x²+4yz=p}. Send (x,y,z) to (x+2z,z,y−x−z) if x<y−z, to (2y−x,y,x−y+z) if y−z<x<2y, and to (x−2y,x−y+z,y) if x>2y. These cases exhaust Sₚ and define an involution with the unique fixed point (1,1,(p−1)/4).

cup-cap.description: For planar points p₁,…,pₖ with strictly increasing x-coordinates, a k-cup has strictly increasing successive slopes, and a k-cap has strictly decreasing successive slopes.

bolzano-weierstrass.description: Every bounded sequence in Euclidean space ℝᵈ has a subsequence converging coordinatewise to a point of ℝᵈ.

dual-sperner-labeling.description: On a barycentric subdivision of the standard n-simplex Δⁿ, n≥1, label vertices by {0,…,n}. A boundary vertex x must receive a label i with xᵢ=0; interior labels are unrestricted.

linear-category.title: k-linear category
linear-category.description: A category whose morphism spaces are vector spaces over a field k and whose composition is k-bilinear. This convention does not require finite sums or a zero object.

categorical-trace.title: Trace in a pivotal monoidal category
categorical-trace.description: Closing an endomorphism using evaluation, coevaluation and the pivotal structure gives its left and right traces, which lie in End(1). They are scalars when End(1) is the ground field; the two traces need not agree.

negligible-morphism.title: Negligible morphism in a spherical linear category
negligible-morphism.description: In a spherical k-linear category with End(1)=k, f:X→Y is negligible if tr(gf)=0 for every g:Y→X. Such morphisms form a tensor ideal.

semisimplification.title: Semisimplification by negligible morphisms
semisimplification.description: Quotient a spherical linear category by its negligible morphisms and take the Karoubi envelope. Under the usual finiteness and nondegeneracy hypotheses this gives a semisimple category; the construction does not guarantee semisimplicity for an arbitrary pivotal category.

semisimple-category.title: Semisimple abelian category
semisimple-category.description: An abelian category in which every object is a finite direct sum of simple objects.

split-simple.title: Split simple object in a k-linear abelian category
split-simple.description: A simple object X in a k-linear abelian category is split if its scalar map k→End(X) is an isomorphism.

split-semisimple.title: Split semisimple k-linear category
split-semisimple.description: A semisimple k-linear abelian category in which every simple object is split.

minimal-idempotent.description: A nonzero idempotent that is not a sum of two nonzero orthogonal idempotents. In a finite-dimensional semisimple algebra A, e is primitive exactly when the left ideal Ae is a simple A-module.

hopf-algebra.description: A unital associative algebra H with coassociative coproduct Δ:H→H⊗H and counit ε:H→k that are algebra homomorphisms, and an antipode S satisfying m(S⊗id)Δ=m(id⊗S)Δ=ηε, where m and η are multiplication and unit.

strong-multiplicity-free.title: Strongly multiplicity-free highest-weight representation
strong-multiplicity-free.description: A finite-dimensional irreducible highest-weight representation of a complex semisimple Lie algebra or its generic Drinfeld–Jimbo quantum group, with one-dimensional weight spaces and weights totally ordered by the root order. The root order compares weights whose difference is a nonnegative integral combination of simple roots.

euler-measure.description: For a compact surface F with finitely many assigned boundary corner angles θᵢ, its Euler measure is e(F)=χ(F)−∑ᵢ(π−θᵢ)/(2π). Smooth portions of the boundary contribute no corner correction.

fusion-category.description: A k-linear semisimple abelian rigid monoidal category with finitely many isomorphism classes of simple objects, finite-dimensional morphism spaces, a k-bilinear tensor product and End(1)=k. Over a non-algebraically closed field, simple objects need not be split.

rational-form.description: For fields k⊂K and a semisimple K-linear abelian tensor category C_K, a rational form over k is a semisimple k-linear abelian tensor category C_k with a tensor equivalence Kar(C_k⊗_k K)≃C_K. The additional tensor structure must be preserved.

complete-rational-form.description: A rational form C_k of C_K for which C_k⊗_k K is already idempotent complete, so C_k⊗_k K≃C_K without adding new summands.

galois-conjugate-category.description: For a fusion category over ℂ with a complete form over a number field k, apply an embedding k→ℂ to its associativity and other structure coefficients and extend scalars to ℂ. This gives a conjugate tensor category, up to tensor equivalence.

frobenius-perron-dimension.title: Frobenius–Perron dimension in a fusion category
frobenius-perron-dimension.description: For a simple object X of a fusion category over ℂ, FPdim(X) is the spectral radius of its fusion matrix, whose entries are multiplicities in X⊗Y. Extend this additively to other objects.

global-dimension.description: For a fusion category over ℂ, the global dimension is the sum of the intrinsic squared norms of its simple objects. For a spherical structure it is the sum of their squared categorical dimensions.

principal-graph.title: Principal graph pair of a finite-index subfactor
principal-graph.description: The pair of rooted bipartite graphs recording tensoring with the generating N–M Hilbert bimodule and its dual. Even vertices are simple N–N or M–M bimodules, odd vertices are simple mixed bimodules, and edge multiplicities count their summands. The graphs may be infinite.

rotational-eigenvector.description: A nonzero n-box S, n>0, satisfying ρ(S)=ωS for the shading-preserving two-click rotation ρ. Since ρⁿ=id, its eigenvalue ω is an nth root of unity.

lopsided-planar-algebra.description: A connected shaded planar algebra, with one-dimensional 0-box spaces, normalized so the shaded contractible circle evaluates to 1. The unshaded circle then evaluates to the index, the product of the two circle moduli.

quantum-integer.description: For n≥1, [n]_q=qⁿ⁻¹+qⁿ⁻³+⋯+q¹⁻ⁿ, and [0]_q=0. Equivalently [n]_q=(qⁿ−q⁻ⁿ)/(q−q⁻¹) when the quotient is defined; the Laurent polynomial also specializes at q=±1.

center-induction.title: Induction to the Drinfeld center of a fusion category
center-induction.description: For a fusion category C over ℂ, the induction functor I:C→Z(C) is the left adjoint to the functor forgetting the half-braiding. Its underlying object is ⊕_V V⊗X⊗V*, summed over simple representatives V.

internal-hom.description: For objects M,N of a module category over C, an internal Hom is an object [M,N] of C with natural bijections Hom_C(X,[M,N])≅Hom_M(X⊗M,N). It exists in the finite semisimple setting used here.

s-matrix.description: For a ribbon fusion category over ℂ, the S-matrix is indexed by simple objects; its (X,Y) entry is the categorical trace of c(Y,X)c(X,Y) on X⊗Y. This is the unnormalized Hopf-link convention.

t-matrix.description: For a ribbon fusion category over ℂ, the T-matrix is diagonal, with entry at a simple object X equal to the scalar of its ribbon twist θ_X. No additional anomaly scalar is included.

modular-category.description: A ribbon fusion category over ℂ whose S-matrix is invertible.

center-base-change.description: In the characteristic-zero fusion-category setting, if C_k is a rational form of C_K, the natural functor Z(C_k)⊗_k K→Z(C_K) is fully faithful, dominant, and commutes with induction. Thus Z(C_k) is a braided rational form, with idempotent completion understood.

module-dual-base-change.description: In the characteristic-zero fusion-category setting, let M_K be an indecomposable finite semisimple module category over D_K and let D_k,M_k be compatible rational forms. Scalar extension induces a fully faithful dominant functor Fun_{D_k}(M_k,M_k)⊗_k K→Fun_{D_K}(M_K,M_K), so the dual category over k is a rational form of the dual over K.

monoidal-natural-transformation.description: A natural transformation between strong monoidal functors compatible with their tensor-product and unit isomorphisms.

additive-category.description: A category with abelian-group morphism sets, composition additive in each variable, a zero object and finite biproducts.

zero-object.description: An object 0 of a category such that for every object X there is exactly one morphism 0→X and exactly one morphism X→0.

biproduct.title: Finite biproduct in a category
biproduct.description: An object with injections and projections making it simultaneously the product and coproduct of a finite family of objects, with the usual compatible identity and zero composites.

tensor-category.description: A k-linear abelian rigid monoidal category with a k-bilinear tensor product and End(1)=k, finite-dimensional morphism spaces, and finite length for every object. Semisimplicity and finitely many simple isomorphism classes are not required.

tensor-ideal.title: Tensor ideal of morphisms in a linear monoidal category
tensor-ideal.description: A family of linear subspaces of morphism spaces closed under composition on either side and tensoring with arbitrary morphisms.

quotient-linear-category.description: For a k-linear category C and a linear ideal I closed under composition on either side, C/I has the same objects and morphism spaces Hom_C(X,Y)/I(X,Y), with induced composition.

fusion-matrix.description: For an object X in a fusion category over ℂ, the matrix (N_X)_{Z,Y} records the multiplicity of the simple object Z in X⊗Y. Rows and columns are indexed by simple isomorphism classes.

grothendieck-ring.description: For a fusion category, the free abelian group on simple isomorphism classes, with addition induced by direct sum and multiplication by tensor product.

squared-norm.title: Intrinsic squared norm of a simple object in a fusion category
squared-norm.description: For a simple X in a fusion category over ℂ, choose an isomorphism a:X→X**. The product Tr(a)Tr((a⁻¹)*) is independent of this choice and is called |X|². With a pivotal structure it equals dim(X)dim(X*).

hilbert-bimodule.description: An M–N Hilbert bimodule is a Hilbert space with commuting normal unital *-representations of von Neumann algebras M and Nᵒᵖ, giving left M and right N actions.

root-of-unity.description: In a field, a root of unity is an element ζ with ζⁿ=1 for some positive integer n; its order is the least such n.

splitting-field-algebra.description: For a finite-dimensional semisimple k-algebra A, a splitting field is an extension K/k for which K⊗_k A is a finite product of full matrix algebras over K.
